title: The Lobby Power Display
transcript: An apartment building put a screen in its lobby to show how much electricity the lifts, corridor lights and shared laundry used. The first version showed the total since the start of the month. Residents told us the rising figure was hard to interpret, so we switched to daily totals beside those for the same day a week earlier. A cleaner noticed that laundry use remained high late at night, even after the room was locked. An electrician found that the dryer fans were running for hours after the machines stopped. A timer adjustment reduced that overnight use, and the next few daily comparisons made the change easy to see.

questions.prompt: How was the screen made easier to interpret?
options: It converted electricity use into an estimated monthly bill.
It ranked the facilities by their share of the total.
It displayed the busiest hour for each facility.
It compared each daily total with the figure from a week earlier.
questions.answer: It compared each daily total with the figure from a week earlier.
questions.explanation: 新版把当天总用电量与上周同一天的数据并列展示。

questions.prompt: How was the overnight electricity use reduced?
options: The laundry was closed earlier in the evening.
The setting that controlled the dryer fans was adjusted.
The dryers were replaced with smaller machines.
The corridor lights were put on motion sensors.
questions.answer: The setting that controlled the dryer fans was adjusted.
questions.explanation: 电工发现烘干机停止后风扇还在运行，调整定时设置后降低了夜间用电。
